# =============================================================================
# STRUCTURE FIXTURE — NOT A MEASUREMENT
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
#   A hand-written input for the mac-exporter powermetrics text parser. It
#   exists to pin the parser's behaviour on the *shape* of the lines it
#   recognizes — "<label>: <number><unit>" — and on its indifference to every
#   other line in the stream.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT
#   It is NOT a capture of powermetrics output from this or any machine, and
#   NONE of the numbers below is a measurement of anything. They were chosen to
#   exercise number formats (integer, decimal, zero) and unit handling, not
#   observed. No test in this crate asserts that any value here describes real
#   hardware; the tests assert only which bytes the parser turns into which
#   field. Do not quote a number from this file anywhere as a power reading,
#   and do not render one in a UI.
#
# WHY IT IS HAND-WRITTEN
#   powermetrics refuses to run without root. Observed on the machine this
#   crate was written on, 2026-08-16, Darwin 25.5.0:
#
#       $ powermetrics --samplers cpu_power -n 1 -i 200
#       powermetrics must be invoked as the superuser
#       $ echo $?
#       1
#
#   This project does not escalate privileges to manufacture a fixture, and it
#   does not invent a capture. So the honest artifact is this one: a parser
#   shape test that claims nothing about hardware. If an operator captures real
#   powermetrics output under the accelerator discipline, it lands beside this
#   file with a PROVENANCE entry, and this file stays exactly what it is.
#
# THE "#" LINES
#   powermetrics has no comment syntax; these lines are not part of the format.
#   The parser ignores every line it does not recognize, and a test asserts
#   that stripping this header changes the parse result not at all.
# =============================================================================
